research: pin: Parley emits every glyph without a control filter (gpui_ce_parley/src/text_system.rs:1267-1287), so a tab paints glyph 0; its width equals a space only in monospace fonts (Consolas 7.70px; Segoe UI 14px tab 9.04px vs space 3.83px)
gpui_elements editable_text (pin and 0.2.2) inserts a real tab (state.rs:1101) and shapes it unexpanded

0.2.2: direct_write.rs:536-555 uses IDWriteTextLayout without SetIncrementalTabStop; a headless dwrite.dll probe showed the default: one blank cluster to the next multiple of 4 x font size from the line start ('a\tb' = 63.697px Consolas, 64.230px Segoe UI at 14px)

gpui-component (c0820693 and the other local checkouts): no tab expansion; TabSize drives indent insertion and indent geometry, which counts a tab as tab_size columns of space width (indent.rs:38-49, 117-137); the whitespace marker draws an arrow at the tab start (text_wrapper.rs:716-742)
Zed's editor TabMap (display_map/tab_map.rs) expands a tab at column c to tab_size - c % tab_size columns; no local Zed tree, so this is from the worker's knowledge, not a local citation

implementation.gpui: ShapeText hands the native service a space in its own one-byte run for each tab (blank, byte offsets unchanged), then stretches it with letter spacing to the next 4 em stop measured from its visual row start (DirectWrite's default), re-shaping up to 4 passes; Relayout re-fits. Matches the DirectWrite measurements to about 0.01px
implementation.base: the input display map follows the tab-map rule: a tab spans tab_size - col % tab_size columns of space width, columns from the buffer line start (also on wrapped rows), using the same one-byte trick so cursor/selection/columns need no mapping; deviation: a click inside a tab snaps to the nearer edge (as 0.2.2's single DirectWrite cluster) where Zed puts it at the start
